jetson_clocks: applied before the run; GPU locked min==max
throttled_evidence: GPU clock sampled before and after all 31 timed rows; observed values [1300500000] Hz against the pinned 1300500000 Hz. Peak GPU die temperature 56.375 C. Per-row samples are columns gpu_hz_* / gpu_C_* / tj_C_after of latency_summary.csv.

measured_peaks._method: CUDA-event timing, median of 100 calls after 20 warm-ups, MAXN, jetson_clocks applied, GPU clock pinned at 1300500000 Hz; every GEMM verified against an fp32 reference before its time was used. See this run's latency_summary.csv.
measured_peaks.peak_int8_CAVEAT: torch._int_mm does not reach the tensor cores on sm_87; this is a PyTorch-path throughput, NOT the hardware's dense INT8 peak. Do not use it as a hardware constant.

efficiency_fractions._purpose: docs/00_context.md carries these as **[ASSUMPTION]** in E11's analytic host model (`achieved_tflops = peak x eff_flops_frac`, `achieved_bw_GBps = ext_bw x eff_bw_frac`). These are the measured values. Both assumptions are pessimistic.
efficiency_fractions._caveat: Measured on dense square GEMM and a streaming kernel — the best case. The action expert's own shapes are small and skinny and do far worse; E2 (micro_ae_kernels.py) measures what THOSE shapes achieve.

notes: Fills the `measured` rows every floor.csv has left empty since T002.
Bandwidth counts read+write for clone and read+read+write for axpy.
Every GEMM was checked against an fp32 reference; `correct` and `rel_err` are per row, and only correct rows were considered for a peak.

int8 via torch._int_mm reaches only ~10 TOP/s, roughly an eighth of the hardware's dense INT8 capability. The result is bit-exact, so this is a kernel-selection limit in PyTorch on sm_87, not a hardware limit. Recorded as a software-path number and explicitly NOT offered as a hardware constant.
bf16 peaks at n=2048 and falls off at n=8192. That is not throttling (the clock never moved and throughput rises with repetition); it is cuBLAS kernel selection at large n.

ANOMALY, unresolved and deliberately NOT used as the constant: the first two bandwidth measurements taken in this session reached 183-190 GB/s on the axpy kernel, and one of them alternated cleanly between ~189 and ~146 GB/s on successive repeats of identical work on identical buffers. That mode could not be reproduced afterwards in roughly 30 further attempts. Ruled out by direct test: GPU clock (pinned at 1300.5 MHz throughout, sampled per row), EMC clock (pinned 3199 MHz, FreqOverride=1), die temperature (148 GB/s at 37 C, colder than the 39 C of the fast run), competing processes (none), accumulated value drift in the accumulator, buffer reuse vs reallocation, caching-allocator pool size and allocation ordering, and re-applying jetson_clocks immediately before measuring. The peak reported here is the reproducible one. Worth re-checking after the power-mode reboots, which clear whatever system state this was.
